meta.title: What this system can DO — capabilities & the decisions it makes for you
meta.version: v2 (re-colored 2026-07-30 from the FIRST real cluster drive — htseq-count + DESeq2 on UNC Longleaf; the amber cells that got exercised now carry real evidence)
meta.purpose: Two maps in one, sharing one inventory. TOP: the action-verbs a user can ask for (install an env, create a pipeline, run data, move bytes, ...) — 'wtf can this thing do'. BOTTOM: every decision the system makes when you don't specify — its default, whether that default is CODED or IMPROVISED, and whether a wrong choice gets caught. This is step one of the determinism plan: you cannot make behaviour deterministic without first enumerating every decision.
meta.honesty_note: v1 is CURATED from reading the code, not auto-swept. Every coded/configurable decision cites its source location so a future drift-lint can verify it (the outcomes-ledger pattern). IMPROVISED decisions have no coded default to verify — they ARE the determinism backlog, not a rendering gap. A capability map that showed only the green would over-promise; the red cells and the one MISSING verb are shown on purpose.

legend.coded_fixed: Hardcoded in the code, no knob. Fully deterministic. (green)
legend.coded_configurable: A stated default in config/signature, overridable. Deterministic with a knob. (blue)
legend.improvised: No coded default — the agent chooses per request. This is the mess-risk surface. (amber)
legend.missing: A capability users will expect that the system does NOT have as a first-class action. (red)

meta.exit_caught_note: exit_caught = does the honesty contract (freeze/seal gates) catch a WRONG choice here? If yes, improvisation is safe (a bad pick can't ship). If no, a wrong choice ships silently — that is where determinism must be enforced up front.

capabilities.ask: Install a tool / build an environment
needs: tool name(s) (versions optional — resolved or asked)
capabilities.produces: a frozen, content-addressed env image + ENV report + recipe + attestation
capabilities.note: The most on-rails verb: tier + build-method + validation are all coded and exit-checked.

capabilities.ask: Add a tool to an environment I already built
capabilities.note: Same rails as install_env, acting on an existing draft.

capabilities.ask: Create & VALIDATE a pipeline (run the steps, prove they work, seal it)
needs: test/validation data (named, or a core dataset is picked)
capabilities.runs_in: test SANDBOX (cluster: scratch/<project>/<workflow>/ ; LOCAL: repo tree — no sandbox yet)
capabilities.produces: a sealed WorkflowSpec + RUN dashboard, rendered purely from the validated run
capabilities.note: This is a COMPOSITION (run_step ×N + the SEAL seam), not a single Kind. It is where the reference/test data (e.g. the GTF) is bound as an ExternalSource. LIMIT surfaced on Longleaf 2026-07-30: a MULTI-STEP CLUSTER chain can't be cleanly SEALED — a step that consumes a prior step's output DIRECTORY (DESeq2 reading htseq-count's counts dir) is an I8 orphan (the directory basename matches no individual file output, and the prior step's outputs are recorded as local download paths). Single-step cluster seal works (proved by samtools_cluster_rung3); directory-aware step->step lineage does not exist yet. Run-and-go is the honest close until it does — forcing the seal would mean declaring step 1's real output as 'external', a REPORTS-NEVER-LIE violation.

capabilities.ask: Run one step against a frozen env
capabilities.produces: validated output files + a recorded pipeline_step
capabilities.note: Authoring-time, single-step, env-centric. NOT production execution of a whole sealed pipeline (see the missing verb).

capabilities.ask: Download reference data (a genome, an annotation, a variant DB)
capabilities.runs_in: LOCAL (background curl) by default; the COMPUTE NODE if a compute_env is named
capabilities.produces: a versioned, sha256-anchored ReferenceDatabase record (local or cluster locus)
capabilities.note: This is the exomiser/GTF question: default is LOCAL; it only goes to the cluster if you say so, and then it lands in the env's shared common_data zone.

capabilities.ask: Move bytes (upload inputs to the cluster / download results back)
needs: remote path (routed by which zone it falls in)
capabilities.produces: verified bytes at the destination + a transfer_history record
capabilities.note: No install implied. Zone + auth are coded; the wire protocol (scp vs globus) is a per-env config knob.

capabilities.ask: Rebuild an env from its recipe and prove it matches
needs: a recipe (yaml) from a prior freeze
capabilities.produces: a rebuilt image + a digest-match verdict
capabilities.note: verify_env_recipe: container-native rebuilds are digest-checked; adopt paths are re-pulled-and-compared; authors-dockerfile refuses (not bit-reproducible).

capabilities.ask: What do I already have / what's on the cluster?
capabilities.runs_in: read-only (local records; one ssh find for a project snapshot)
capabilities.produces: the frozen envs + sealed workflows on disk; a one-level cluster dir walk
capabilities.note: Query-only. contract_ok is re-earned at read time, not remembered.

capabilities.ask: Run MY real data through an already-sealed pipeline, with my params
capabilities.produces: results in the user's project workspace
capabilities.note: THE HOLE. Production execution exists only as the HPC bridge submit_workflow_job, not as a modeled verb. And nothing checks that the reference/inputs a production run binds match what the pipeline was SEALED against — the reference rebind is currently ungoverned.

decisions.question: Where does the work run — local or cluster?
decisions.source: emergent from which primitive the agent calls; the only STATED policy (Compute.unspecified, 'never silently defaulted to local') lives in the advisory intent layer
decisions.note: A wrong locus still seals honestly — the exit contract has nothing to say about it. Top of the determinism backlog. Exercised end-to-end on Longleaf 2026-07-30 (both steps ran cluster-locus via run_step_on_cluster; the choice was mine, not modeled).

decisions.question: Where is the container image actually BUILT?
decisions.source: docker buildx build on the local daemon; no cluster-build path by design (never build on a head node — build local, ship via apptainer)
decisions.note: The decision the capability list originally hid. Hardcoded, with a strong rationale ([[feedback-no-head-node-image-builds]]). Deterministic.

decisions.question: Which install path (conda / pip / cran / author-image / authors-recipe / binary / source / ...)?
decisions.source: resolve_tool's reliability-gated ranked ladder (author_image > authors_recipe > conda > pip/cran/bioc > binary > synthesis > source > manual)
decisions.note: The most deterministic decision in the system. A wrong tier is caught at freeze (VALIDATED_IN_IMAGE).

decisions.question: Adopt a published biocontainer, or build the image from scratch?
decisions.default: pure-conda + a published biocontainer -> ADOPT by digest; anything else -> container-native BUILD
decisions.note: Coded and exit-checked (the built/adopted image must pass the honesty contract).

decisions.question: What target architecture is the image built for?
decisions.note: On an arm64 host, amd64 builds/runs are QEMU-emulated — I7 timings are then marked non-authoritative (locus: emulated). BUG surfaced+fixed on Longleaf 2026-07-30: a container-native env records platform in CONDA form ('linux-64') while adopt/authors records use DOCKER form ('linux/amd64'); stage_apptainer fed the conda form straight into `docker --platform` and hard-failed (the first build-archive .sif ever staged to a cluster hit this). Fixed by canonicalizing at the docker boundary. The record's dual spelling remains a cosmetic report inconsistency worth reconciling.

decisions.question: What OS base does a container-native build start from?
decisions.source: container_build.BASE_IMAGE (digest-pinned for OS-layer reproducibility). NB: config docker.base_image says 'ubuntu:22.04' — a separate/legacy path, a dual-source worth reconciling
decisions.note: Digest-pinned = deterministic. Flagged: two sources name a base image; only the hardcoded one drives the container-native build.

decisions.question: Which conda channels are searched, in what order?
decisions.note: Channel order is deterministic; a package resolving from an unexpected channel is still exit-validated in-image.

decisions.question: What Python does a fresh env get when unspecified?
Where does downloaded reference data go — local or cluster?
decisions.default: LOCAL (local_path); cluster only if compute_env is named
decisions.note: The exomiser/GTF answer: local by default, explicit knob to send it to the cluster.

decisions.question: HOW is the reference actually fetched?
decisions.default: curl -L --progress-bar -C - (resumable) in background locally; a resumable wget -c/curl -C - SLURM job on the compute node if cluster-directed
decisions.note: Resumable both ways. The head node never pulls a giant DB — the compute node does.

decisions.question: Where on the cluster does a directed reference land?
Where does env/pipeline CREATION & VALIDATION write?
decisions.default: cluster: ALWAYS scratch/<project>/<workflow>/ (no caller knob); LOCAL: the repo tree (envs/, env_reports/) — NO sandbox
decisions.source: cluster half is coded (run_step_on_cluster); local half has no sandbox — the parity gap you flagged
decisions.note: PARITY GAP. The test-dir/project-dir split is a locus-INDEPENDENT policy that today holds only on the cluster. Bringing local into parity converts this cell to coded. CLUSTER HALF CONFIRMED on Longleaf 2026-07-30: scratch/<project>/<workflow>/ is auto-computed with no caller knob and worked cleanly for both steps. The LOCAL sandbox is the remaining actionable item (user-blessed).

decisions.question: Where does a PRODUCTION run write its outputs?
decisions.default: cluster: directories[] (explicit per-dir auth); LOCAL: undefined
decisions.source: cluster half coded via projects_access.yaml directories[]; local production has no defined zone
decisions.note: Other half of the parity policy: execution -> project dirs. Cluster-only today.

decisions.question: How much time / memory / cpus does a cluster job request?
decisions.default: time & mem REQUIRED (no default); cpus/ntasks default to 1
decisions.source: _check_slurm requires time+mem; the agent must supply them (today: a guess, or derived from non-authoritative emulated numbers)
decisions.note: The system refuses to FABRICATE a measured number, but the REQUESTED sizing is an unprincipled agent guess. Too low -> OOM kill; too high -> waste. No profile-then-size loop exists. FIRST AUTHORITATIVE DATA (Longleaf 2026-07-30): htseq-count requested 8G/30min, really used 488MB/44s (~16x over on mem); DESeq2 requested 4G/20min, really used 1.28GB/25s (~3x over). Both jobs succeeded — the guess erred SAFE (over-provisioned), so this cell costs efficiency, not correctness. A data-informed default (a per-tool table seeded from sacct MaxRSS/Elapsed, or a profile-then-size loop) is now concrete and unblocked.

decisions.question: What data validates the pipeline?
decisions.default: you name it; else the agent picks from data/core_test_data_hg38/manifest.yaml
decisions.note: If specified, deterministic and bound as an ExternalSource. Unspecified -> agent chooses; the choice is at least exit-validated as a real typed input.

decisions.question: How is heavy test data trimmed to stay fast?
decisions.default: max 10000 reads; restrict to chr22 (fallback chr1)

decisions.question: How is the frozen image delivered to HPC?
decisions.default: registry-free: docker save -> apptainer build docker-archive (zero config); a registry push if config docker.registry or push_target is set
decisions.note: Gated (licensed) artifacts are never pushed (I13) — tarball-only.

decisions.question: GPU/accelerator policy for the env?
decisions.source: freeze() accel='none'; GPU base nvidia/cuda:12.1.0 when gpu_required
decisions.note: I12 accelerator honesty: cuda/rocm need a toolkit_version; runtime_verified needs a captured probe.

decisions.question: Is the artifact license-gated (not redistributable)?
decisions.note: I13 license firewall: gated => redistributable:false AND licenses[] recorded, never pushed.

decisions.question: How do bytes move to/from the cluster?
decisions.default: scp_head_node (scp + sha256 round-trip); globus if the env declares it

decisions.question: Which directory is scanned for a step's outputs?
decisions.note: An output written elsewhere with no watch_dir override is undetected -> unvalidated -> fails I3 at seal. So a wrong default is exit-caught (loudly).

decisions.question: At production run time, is the bound reference checked against what the pipeline was SEALED against?
decisions.source: submit_workflow_job takes concrete input paths; nothing diffs them against the sealed spec's pinned references
decisions.note: REPORTS-NEVER-LIE gap: a pipeline validated against gencode.v44 can be run against gencode.v38 and nothing discloses the divergence. The data analog of the tool requested-vs-installed drift flag we already enforce.
